name: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
notes: TLS 1.3 names only the symmetric half; key exchange and authentication are negotiated separately

name: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
notes: the SHA-384 is the HKDF/PRF hash not a MAC; GCM authenticates by itself

name: TLS_AES_128_CCM_8_SHA256
notes: tag truncated to 8 bytes so forgery resistance drops to about 2^64; the only TLS 1.3 suite not recommended

name: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
notes: TLS 1.2 names the whole bundle including key exchange and authentication

name: TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_CTR_OMAC
notes: TLS 1.2; a national standard replaces the whole symmetric layer not just the signature

name: TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_28147_CNT_IMIT
notes: TLS 1.2; the 1989 cipher kept for compatibility

name: TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_MGM_L
notes: TLS 1.3 with GOST does not use the TLS_AES or CHACHA20 suites; L and S differ in how much key material is used before rekeying (TLSTREE)

name: TLS_GOSTR341112_256_WITH_KUZNYECHIK_MGM_S
notes: TLS 1.3; S is the shorter rekeying interval
